first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses both the completion decline and likely upstream pressure on activation, without immediately risking margin quality. Verify memory_86 because its evidence stops at early adoption, and memory_73 because promotional pricing is the strongest competing response but its claimed revenue lift may not establish durable retention, margin, or customer quality under the long-term qualified-revenue objective.

mid.rationale: Run a standard onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified source shows materially higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, aligning with both current declines and sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite acquisition lift because its cohort suffered 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. The experiment should still validate that the prior onboarding gains generalize to the current population.

final2.rationale: Continue with onboarding simplification. The verified evidence shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, supporting sustainable qualified revenue while addressing current onboarding and activation weakness. The competitor escalation increases urgency but does not overturn verified evidence that a 40% targeted discount attracted a cohort with 12% lower retention that failed to survive renewal. Price-related churn remains an acute risk, but neither promotional pricing nor the other unverified directions has stronger evidence for sustainable retention this cycle.
